short: Investigation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy for potential application
title: Investigation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy for potential application of biodegradable esophageal stent material

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: 317L SS esophageal stents are hard, cause extra injury and pain, and do not inhibit the cells that drive restenosis. A soft, biodegradable Mg-based alloy should outperform 317L SS as an esophageal stent: degrade, alkalise the site and inhibit pathological cells.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Degradation opens a porous surface on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd that coarsens into a deep cellular network by 22-30 days; 317L SS stays flat

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd degrades far faster than 317L SS: much lower corrosion potential, ~3 decades higher corrosion current, higher immersion corrosion rate. Mg dissolution consumes water and releases hydroxide (Mg + 2H2O -> Mg2+ + 2OH- + H2), so degrading Mg alkalises the medium.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (PRP/value), n8 (MEC/pathway), n9 (PRP/value), n11 (PRP/value), n12 (PRP/value). Premises: Mg corrodes in aqueous media by Mg + 2H2O -> Mg(OH)2 + H2, raising local pH

states.title: Performance state
states.head: A degrading Mg-Zn-Y-Nd stent could neutralise the acidic esophageal tumour environment, an advantage over 317L SS. Mg-Zn-Y-Nd should suppress the cancer, fibroblast, squamous and inflammatory cells that cause stent restenosis
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (PRF/service_capability), n16 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: The focus of advanced esophageal cancer is chronically acidic because of inflammation and canceration; Eca109, L929 and Het-1A cells participate in esophageal stent restenosis; macrophages are the main inflammatory cells

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd is a promising biodegradable esophageal stent material with advantages over 317L SS

nodes.title: SEM, F4
nodes.head: SEM: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd shows pits by 3 d, patchy attack at 7-10 d, a pitted then deep cellular network at 15-30 d; 317L SS stays flat at all times
nodes.solves: Degradation opens a porous surface on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd that coarsens into a deep cellular network by 22-30 days; 317L SS stays flat
nodes.note: progression is not monotonic: the 10 d panel looks less attacked than 7 d; scale bars unreadable, so pore size cannot be measured
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown and n6 has no other figure-backed support.

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Water contact angle ranks Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (59.9 +/- 1.2 deg) above 317L SS (28.4 +/- 2.7 deg); inset droplets agree
nodes.solves: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd is less wettable than 317L SS: water contact angle about 60 vs 28 degrees
nodes.note: inset droplet photos: taller cap on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd, flatter on 317L SS
nodes.detail: o4: Water contact angle ranks Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (59.9 +/- 1.2 deg) above 317L SS (28.4 +/- 2.7 deg); inset droplets agree
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n11 (o4).

nodes.title: ECHEM:potentiodynamic, F3, F5
nodes.head: Polarization curves: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd corrosion potential near -1.5 V vs about -0.25 V for 317L SS, its branches 2-3 decades to higher current. Inset table: Ecorr -1.49 vs -0.25 V, Icorr 24.93 vs 0.017 uA/cm2, Zre 8450 vs 75190 ohm/cm2 (Mg-Zn-Y-Nd vs 317L SS).
nodes.solves: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd degrades far faster than 317L SS: much lower corrosion potential, ~3 decades higher corrosion current, higher immersion corrosion rate
nodes.op: compare across conditions, fit model, read characteristic point
nodes.note: x axis carries tick values -11 to -1 but no label (presumably log current density); medium SBF is caption-only Zre unit printed as ohm/cm2 (should be ohm cm2); 8450/75190 gives the 88.76% drop quoted in text Mg error bars are wide (day 1: ~0.09-0.37 mm/y); rate method not stated in the packet
nodes.detail: o5: Polarization curves: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd corrosion potential near -1.5 V vs about -0.25 V for 317L SS, its branches 2-3 decades to higher current; o6: Inset table: Ecorr -1.49 vs -0.25 V, Icorr 24.93 vs 0.017 uA/cm2, Zre 8450 vs 75190 ohm/cm2 (Mg-Zn-Y-Nd vs 317L SS); o10: Immersion corrosion rate of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (0.13-0.38 mm/y, peak at day 7) stays above 317L SS (<0.07 mm/y) at every time point
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n7 (o5, o6, o10).

nodes.title: ASSAY, F5
nodes.head: pH with Mg-Zn-Y-Nd climbs from 7.4 to ~10 by day 22 and plateaus; blank control peaks ~8.4 then falls to ~7.5; 317L SS falls to ~6.1 at day 20
nodes.solves: Immersed Mg-Zn-Y-Nd drives Hank's solution to pH ~10 and holds it there, above the blank control; 317L SS does not
nodes.note: text says Mg pH rises within 16 days; the plot keeps rising to ~day 22
nodes.detail: o8: pH with Mg-Zn-Y-Nd climbs from 7.4 to ~10 by day 22 and plateaus; blank control peaks ~8.4 then falls to ~7.5; 317L SS falls to ~6.1 at day 20
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n9 (o8).

nodes.title: ASSAY:stain, F6, F7, F8, F9
nodes.head: AO/EB images: fewer stained cells on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd than on 317L SS in most panels; the gap is widest at 3 d, where SS is dense. Vital-cell ratio is lower on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (about 74-88%) than on 317L SS (about 87-98%) at every time for all four cell types.
nodes.solves: Fewer cells adhere and fewer remain vital on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd than on 317L SS in all four cell cultures
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: macrophages at 4 h (F9a) and L929 at 1 d (F7a) show comparable counts on both metals; Eca109 on Mg at 3 d (F6a) carries many small green/yellow punctate specks (debris or fragmented cells?); SS at 3 d is confluent for Eca109/L929, dense or clustered for Het-1A/macrophages text says Mg-Zn-Y-Nd had 'significantly lower vital ratios' for all four types a few yellow dots on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd at 1-3 d (F6a) only; the 12-26% non-vital fraction is read from the ratio panels in o12 (F6b-F9b)
nodes.detail: o11: AO/EB images: fewer stained cells on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd than on 317L SS in most panels; the gap is widest at 3 d, where SS is dense; o12: Vital-cell ratio is lower on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (about 74-88%) than on 317L SS (about 87-98%) at every time for all four cell types; o13: Differences are not starred for L929 and Het-1A at 72 h or macrophages at 4 h; Mg-Zn-Y-Nd ratios stay at 74-88%; o15: AO/EB images show almost only green cells; no red EB-stained dead cells matching the 12-26% non-vital fraction are visible
nodes.inner_audit: o15: a few yellow dots on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd at 1-3 d (F6a) only; the 12-26% non-vital fraction is read from the ratio panels in o12 (F6b-F9b)
nodes.necessity_reason: Changes support for S2: o11 partial

nodes.title: MICRO, F8, F9
nodes.head: On Mg-Zn-Y-Nd, Het-1A and macrophage numbers rise from 1 d to 3 d rather than falling
nodes.solves: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd should suppress the cancer, fibroblast, squamous and inflammatory cells that cause stent restenosis
nodes.note: text says pathological cell numbers on Mg-Zn-Y-Nd 'decreased gradually or maintained at a lower value'; judge: the original clause 'only Eca109 and L929 stay sparse' was dropped: L929 (F7a) is not cited on this node and Eca109 at 3 d (F6a) shows many punctate specks, so it is not clearly sparse

nodes.title: ASSAY, F5
nodes.head: 317L SS pH tracks near the blank until day ~9, then falls well below it and recovers to ~7.1 by day 30
nodes.solves: A degrading Mg-Zn-Y-Nd stent could neutralise the acidic esophageal tumour environment, an advantage over 317L SS
nodes.note: an acidification by passive steel below the blank is not explained; part of the Mg vs SS pH gap is this SS drop, not Mg alkalisation alone; before day 9 SS sits at or up to ~0.5 below the blank (day 1: 7.8 vs 8.3), the sharp divergence starts at day 9-10; text says SS stays under pH 7.0 to day 30, the plot reads ~7.05 at day 30
nodes.detail: o9: 317L SS pH tracks near the blank until day ~9, then falls well below it and recovers to ~7.1 by day 30
nodes.inner_audit: o9: an acidification by passive steel below the blank is not explained; part of the Mg vs SS pH gap is this SS drop, not Mg alkalisation alone; before day 9 SS sits at or up to ~0.5 below the blank (day 1: 7.8 vs 8.3), the sharp divergence starts at day 9-10; text says SS stays under pH 7.0 to day 30, the plot reads ~7.05 at day 30

nodes.title: MECH:hardness, F1, F2
nodes.head: Height maps: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd flat within ~1 um with parallel polishing lines; 317L SS flat apart from scattered deep pits. Roughness 57.08 +/- 4.65 nm for Mg-Zn-Y-Nd vs 32.20 +/- 3.63 nm for 317L SS.
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: colour scales span -0.9 to 0.4 um (Mg) and -2.2 to 3.0 um (SS); the SS 3D view is saturated red, so the larger SS height range comes from a few deep pits bar heights agree with the printed value labels; roughness parameter (Ra/Sa) not named on the panel; text quotes +/-4.05 nm, the panel prints +/-4.65
nodes.detail: o1: Height maps: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd flat within ~1 um with parallel polishing lines; 317L SS flat apart from scattered deep pits; o2: Roughness 57.08 +/- 4.65 nm for Mg-Zn-Y-Nd vs 32.20 +/- 3.63 nm for 317L SS; o3: Microhardness ranks 317L SS (198.7 +/- 9.9 HV) far above Mg-Zn-Y-Nd (54.3 +/- 2.5 HV)
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n17 (o1, o2, o3).
